newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric gains on bid defence.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric gains on bid defence.

text.p: Shares in Northern Electric Plc rose on Tuesday after the company bolstered its bid defences with plans to merge its supply businesses with another, unnamed, regional electricity company (Rec) and forecast a sharp rise in its fiscal 1998 dividend.
The stock was up 9-1/2p at 615 by 0824 GMT.
"It's a fairly agressive statement from Northern Electric showing they're preparing yet again to gear up to the gunwales," said Yamaichi utilities and transport analyst Nigel Hawkins.

Northern, fending off a 650p-per-share bid fron CE Electric, forecast a 17 percent rise in its 1998 dividend to 50p per share and predicted joint annual savings of 28 million stg if it merged its electricity and gas supply businesses with those of another Rec.
It said its dividend would subsequently rise by seven percent a year from its new higher level.
Hawkins said the imminent decision from Board of Trade president Ian Lang on whether to send CE Electric's bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission remained the crucial issue.
"(Today's announcement) is seen as a slight side issue. By far the most important thing is Lang's decision expected by next Monday," he said.
Hawkins said investors would probably take up CE Electric's offer as political and market uncertainty tempts them to cash in near term rather than look to the longer run.
"If Lang allows the bid to proceed, I would have thought CE Electric remains in poll position," said Hawkins.
